promise: "AI that can match humans at any task will be here in five to 10 years"
description: Hassabis repeatedly predicted AGI in roughly a 5-10 year window, later tightening to 'around 2030, possibly as early as 2029' (May 2026 interviews). Long-dated timeline, still pending and unverifiable.
evidence: Nov 2025: Hassabis reiterated 5-10 years (Times of India)
May 2026: 'DeepMind CEO predicts AGI in 2030' (Axios); 'as early as 2029' (GIGAZINE)

promise: Reduce the net carbon intensity of our energy products by 20% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, versus 2016 (net zero by 2050).
description: Shell's 2021 Energy Transition Strategy set 20% (2030) and 45% (2035) intensity cuts. On 14 June 2023 CEO Wael Sawan scrapped the 2035 target outright and cut the 2030 target to 9-12% - the most high-profile corporate climate target reversal of its era (reneged before the deadline).
evidence: 14 June 2023 update: 2035 target removed; 2030 target weakened from 20% to 9-12%
Sawan also dropped Shell's plan to reduce oil production every year through the decade (Wikipedia: Wael Sawan)
Court-ordered 45% cut (Milieudefensie) later overturned on appeal, Nov 2024

promise: Raise defence spending to 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defence plus 1.5% for defence-related projects)
description: At the June 2025 summit in The Hague, NATO leaders replaced the 2% Wales target with a 5%-of-GDP target to be achieved by 2035, split into 3.5% for core defence and 1.5% for defence-related projects. As of mid-2026, five Allies were projected to already exceed the 3.5% core target, while most remained below it and one Ally still spent under 2%.
evidence: Target of 5% of GDP by 2035 adopted at The Hague Summit (June 2025)
July 2026 NATO figures: only five Allies projected above the 3.5% core target

role: Parties to the UNFCCC Paris Agreement
promise: Provide at least $300 billion per year in climate finance to developing countries by 2035, with $1.3 trillion as the overall ambition
description: At COP29 in Baku, parties adopted a New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance: at least $300 billion per year by 2035, with developed countries taking the lead and a wider goal of $1.3 trillion annually from all sources, tripling the previous $100 billion goal.
evidence: NCQG decision adopted at COP29 (Nov 2024): at least $300bn/year by 2035
Aspirational goal of $1.3 trillion per year from all sources set alongside the floor

promise: Canada will meet NATO's new Defence Investment Pledge of 5% of GDP by 2035, and double defence expenditures with an additional C$80 billion over five years
description: Canada joined the NATO Defence Investment Pledge agreed at the 2025 Hague Summit to invest 5% of annual GDP in defence and defence-related spending by 2035. Prime Minister Mark Carney reaffirmed the commitment in February 2026, pledging to double defence expenditures by the end of the decade with an additional C$80 billion over five years, and Canada said it would hit NATO's 2% target in 2026.
evidence: Canada joined the new NATO Defence Investment Pledge on June 25, 2025
Carney reaffirmed doubling defence spending and the 5% by 2035 target in February 2026

promise: Achieve carbon neutrality across the entire battery value chain by 2035, with supplier carbon-footprint data required from 2027
description: At a launch event in Ningde on August 18, 2026, CATL announced it had achieved its 2025 carbon-neutrality target for core operations, with all 20 of its battery plants receiving carbon-neutral certification, and outlined a roadmap to carbon neutrality across its entire value chain by 2035. The company published procurement guidelines requiring suppliers to provide carbon footprint data from 2027, with favorable terms offered to suppliers accelerating decarbonization.
evidence: Launch event in Ningde, August 18, 2026; 2025 core-operation target achieved
2035 value-chain goal with supplier carbon-footprint data required from 2027
